text:
nina: We need a lightweight invariant: at any millisecond, the router's routing decision should nominate exactly one primary variant for non-proxyable requests. Right now proxies sometimes forward to both during transitions. Thoughts on a simple protocol?
harry: agreed. For non-idempotent requests we must guarantee single-primary. I propose we adopt a fast-path lease token: router holds token T which is valid for short windows. Escort endorses token via signed ack. If router doesn't have valid token, it cannot route to new variant for non-idempotent reqs.
ci-bot: CI: rolling smoke for canary-4
sec-team: signed tokens are fine, but check key access patterns; we should avoid synchronous KMS calls on path. Have escort sign with cluster key asynchronously.
nina: right. We'll cache signed token in router control-plane and rotate every 500ms. 
harry: for fallback, escort will publish 'release intent' messages. Router will accept either explicit RELEASE token or expiry. Also maintain a per-request header `X-RI-lease` so proxies can detect and drop duplicate routing locally.
oncall: oncall: add runbook note: if dual-serve seen, run `ri diagnostics lease-scan` to list mismatched leases across routers/escorts.
ci-bot: CI: canary progressed to 5%
sec-team: also add nonce to signed token to prevent replay. Use AEAD for token envelope.
nina: plan: proto + token lifecycle docs. Harry will handle router cache + header enforcement. Oncall to add diagnostics. Security to do key rotation design.
harry: small optimization: routers subscribe to escort status via ephemeral websocket to avoid control-plane DB hops on each flip.
nina: agreed. We'll do websocket subscription with resync every 30s. 
ci-bot: canary: no errors so far
harry: TL;DR: single-primary invariant via short-lived signed lease tokens + per-request header + diagnostics + force-release.
nina: adding RFC to track. reviewers: @harry @sec-team @oncall.
harry: ack
sec-team: ack
oncall: ack
nina: thanks :white_check_mark:
